p.PERSONAL-PLAN: A contributor's adaptive plan, cursor, custody and handoffs are local. They may change many times per day without generating repository conflicts or dictating another contributor's workflow.

p.SHARED-CONTRACT: A repository campaign document is optional and deliberately shared. When present, it carries stable mandate, interfaces, integration gates and owner decisions. A named campaign integrator owns its mutable projection. Contributors propose changes through branches/PRs or uniquely named records; they do not all edit one status line.

p.UNIQUE-PATH: Concurrent contribution, finding, decision-proposal and acceptance-evidence records use a path containing campaign id, contributor id and a UUID or sufficiently strong timestamp+nonce. No shared sequence number is allocated. Two writers choosing independently cannot select the same path.

p.DERIVED-INDEX: Indexes and dashboards are pure deterministic projections over records and repository state. They are regenerated by the integrator or tooling; no contributor hand-edits a derived index. A project that cannot regenerate an index does not call it derived.

p.NO-REPO-PERSONAL-CONTINUE: A root `CONTINUE.md`, global mutable WAL, shared personal `TASKS.md`, or branch-agnostic agent mode file is not a multi-contributor handoff channel. Migrate personal continuity local; retain a repo-level status file only when a named integrator owns it as a shared projection.

tr.td: The producer says its packet passed. Evidence only.
The contributor-central read the diff/artifact against mandate and architecture.
Required exact tests, negative proofs and hygiene gates reproduced in the contributor's integration tree.
A repository reviewer assessed the proposed shared change and evidence.
The change is present in the integration branch; merge is location, not automatically semantic closure.
The owner/integrator's declared campaign gates passed and shared status may advance.

p.TIER-NO-INFERENCE: Never infer a higher tier from a lower one. A green worker report is not central review; a commit is not a passing gate; a merge is not proof that the campaign exit criteria hold. Roles may collapse in a one-person project, but the evidence transitions remain explicit.

facts.ACCEPT-ARCH: Compare the complete artifact to owner mandate, governing specs, architecture and its planned write perimeter.
facts.ACCEPT-DIFF: Read the actual diff/content; verify no unrelated, hidden, generated or worker-authority changes arrived.
facts.ACCEPT-GATES: Run exact tests and negative proofs proportional to the risk. Use broad/full panels at integration boundaries, public-surface waves and final closure, not reflexively after every atom.
facts.ACCEPT-MEMORY: Promote stable discoveries into durable project homes and record remaining uncertainty explicitly.
facts.ACCEPT-PLAN: Only then move the node and acceptance tier, re-evaluate dependencies, reproject the plan and decide whether cleanup is safe.

p.PROMOTION-QUEUE: Every local finding is classified as `ephemeral | machine-local | candidate-project-fact | candidate-decision | candidate-work | accepted-project-fact`. Candidates name their evidence and governing anchor. Acceptance chooses the permanent home; it does not paste a whole worker report into a specification.

p.PROMOTION-HOMES: Use the narrowest durable home: normative requirement in PROP/FEAT/flow; executable contract in tests; public usage in docs/examples; open future work in a uniquely named issue or backlog record; contributor preference or machine launcher fact in user-local state. The repository stores what another contributor needs, not every detail one session observed.

p.FORK-LAW: A fork carries project authority through commits and shared records, not the contributor's `~/.vibe/steward` directory. The contributor may export a human-reviewed handoff as a PR artifact only when the project asks for it; local custody and model/session metadata are normally irrelevant to review.

p.INTEGRATOR-RECONCILES: The campaign integrator reconciles concurrent contributions against the shared mandate and integration gates. Git conflict resolution never silently chooses semantic authority; contradictory changes become an explicit decision or REVIEW item.
